extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI (self-assessment using the provider's own QMS), or third-party assessment of QMS and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (e.g., biometric identification), Annex VII assessment by a notified body is required where harmonised standards or common specifications have not been fully applied; where they have been applied, the provider may choose internal control or notified body assessment.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Annex I Section A (e.g., machinery, medical devices), the provider must follow the relevant third-party conformity assessment procedure under that sectoral legislation, with the notified body also verifying AI-specific requirements.

The provider may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or Union bodies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body instead.

Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, unless the changes were predetermined by the provider at the time of the initial assessment (relevant to continuously-learning systems).

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by derogation from Article 43, the placing on the market of a specific high-risk AI system for a limited period for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental or key infrastructure protection, without completing the standard conformity assessment.

Annex VII 4.5 gives notified bodies, as a last resort and upon reasoned request, the right to access the training and trained models (including parameters) of an AI system to verify conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the system of identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies designated under the AI Act.

A Council document references an Article 30 designation-of-conformity-assessment-bodies scope and a coding system (AIP codes) tied to Annex I categories of AI systems for use in the NANDO information system.

A proposed Commission regulation (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 COD) would add a new Annex XIV listing categories of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO notified/designated body system and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.

As of October 2025, NANDO lists 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR), but these are sectoral medical-device designations, not AI Act designations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act for medical device/SaMD conformity assessment.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity.

A news source states that post-2026, notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, implying none had been designated as of that publication.

Under the Cyber Resilience Act (a separate but related regulation), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO, with a target of sufficient capacity by 11 December 2026 and full application from 11 December 2027.

An original 2021 Commission proposal text of Article 43 required providers of Annex III point 1 high-risk systems to follow a conformity assessment procedure based on internal control or one involving a notified body, depending on application of harmonised standards.

One legal-analysis source states that the final text agreed in September 2026 moved the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 August 2029, replacing an earlier date of 2 December 2027 that itself had been set by an 'AI Omnibus' amendment to Article 113, citing lack of readiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.
The same sources state that until 2 August 2029, providers of Annex III high-risk systems do not need a conformity assessment by a notified body.

Other sources (compliance guides and blogs) continue to treat 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline by which high-risk AI obligations, conformity assessment, CE marking and declarations of conformity must be completed, with no mention of any 2027 or 2029 deferral.

The Commission's AI Act Service Desk's official outline of Section 5 (Articles 40-49) lists the full suite of conformity-assessment-related provisions: harmonised standards (40), common specifications (41), presumption of conformity (42), conformity assessment (43), certificates (44), notified body information obligations (45), derogation (46), EU declaration of conformity (47), CE marking (48), and registration obligations (49).

contradictions.claim_a: The final text agreed in September 2026 moved the Annex III high-risk obligations deadline to 2 August 2029, replacing the earlier 2 December 2027 date, due to unready standards and notified bodies.
contradictions.claim_b: Multiple 2026-dated industry/compliance sources state the operative deadline for high-risk AI obligations, conformity assessment and CE marking remains 2 August 2026, with no reference to any extension to 2027 or 2029.
contradictions.description: Sources disagree on the applicable deadline for Annex III high-risk AI conformity assessment obligations: some claim it has been deferred to 2029 (via an intermediate 2027 date), while others (including sources published in 2026) still treat 2 August 2026 as the binding deadline. This is a significant, unresolved discrepancy about EU law's current state, and the 'deferral' sources are not official EU legal texts but legal-analysis/blog commentary, which the official EU guidance sources do not corroborate.

contradictions.claim_a: As of April 2026, no notified bodies were formally designated under the AI Act (source 23); as of March 2026 the notified body ecosystem was still being built with no designations reported (source 22).
contradictions.claim_b: Source 24 implies notified-body AI Act assessments would only begin 'post-2026,' consistent with no designations yet, but other official sources (8, 9, 25) describe active regulatory machinery (Article 35 lists, Article 30 designation scope, proposed Annex XIV) without clarifying whether any notified bodies have actually been designated under the AI Act as of the sources' dates.
contradictions.description: There is ambiguity/inconsistency between sources that explicitly state zero AI Act notified bodies have been designated as of early-to-mid 2026, and official EU procedural sources describing an active designation framework (Article 30, Article 35, proposed Annex XIV) without confirming whether this framework has yet produced any actual designated notified bodies.

open_issues: No source provides a definitive, authoritative (official EU legal text or Commission NANDO database) confirmation of whether any notified bodies have actually been designated under the AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) as of October 2026, nor how many, nor their names/scopes.

The conflicting claims about the Annex III high-risk deadline (2 August 2026 vs. 2 December 2027 vs. 2 August 2029) are not resolved by any official EUR-Lex or Council legal text in the provided sources; it is unclear which date is currently legally binding.
It is unclear from the sources whether the proposed amendments in COM(2025) 836 (new Annex XIV, NANDO integration, amendment to Regulation 2018/1139) have been formally adopted or remain a proposal.

The relationship and overlap between Article 30 (designation of conformity assessment bodies, referenced in source 8) and Article 35 (identification numbers and lists of notified bodies) is not explained in detail across the sources.

Sources do not clarify how many, if any, Member States have completed the formal process of designating notified bodies specifically for AI Act purposes, as opposed to MDR/IVDR or other sectoral notified bodies.

The sources do not specify what capacity or timeline constraints (beyond general statements of 'limited capacity' and 'ongoing processes') exist for notified body designation specifically under the AI Act, unlike the more detailed CRA timeline given for comparison.

It remains unclear whether harmonised standards referenced in Article 40 (needed to establish presumption of conformity and determine which assessment route applies) have been finalized, which affects which systems require notified-body involvement under Annex VII versus self-assessment under Annex VI.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems under Article 43, combining internal control with third-party notified body review, with Article 30 and Article 35 providing the designation framework and coding system for conformity assessment bodies ([Council of the EU, ST-7322-2026](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). However, significant uncertainty persists regarding both the applicable timeline and whether any notified bodies have actually been designated. While the Commission has built procedural infrastructure (Articles 30, 35, and a proposed Annex XIV), no source in this research confirms actual operational notified bodies under the AI Act, and conflicting accounts exist about whether the relevant deadline is 2 August 2026 or has been deferred to 2029.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 establishes two primary pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI (self-assessment using the provider's quality management system) or third-party assessment of QMS and technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For Annex III point 1 systems (e.g., biometric identification), notified body assessment under Annex VII is mandatory where harmonised standards or common specifications have not been fully applied; where applied, providers may choose either route (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)).

For systems already covered by sectoral EU product-safety legislation (Annex I Section A, e.g., machinery, medical devices), providers must follow that sector's existing third-party conformity assessment procedure, with the notified body additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)).

### Notified Body Selection and Powers
Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII procedures, except where the system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union bodies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs this role instead (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Notified bodies retain a last-resort right under Annex VII 4.5 to access training data and trained model parameters to verify conformity, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Modifications, Derogations, and Legal Framework
Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment unless pre-determined by the provider at initial assessment (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise market placement without full conformity assessment for limited periods on public security or health grounds (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). A Council document references Article 30's designation-of-conformity-assessment-bodies scope and an "AIP code" system tied to Annex I categories of AI systems, intended for use in the Commission's NANDO information system (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU, ST-7322-2026](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). Article 35 separately establishes the framework for identification numbers and public lists of designated notified bodies (low confidence) ([Regulation-AI.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
No source confirms any notified bodies have actually been designated under the AI Act. By contrast, NANDO lists 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies as of October 2025—but these are sectoral medical-device designations, not AI Act designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Multiple lower-confidence sources state that as of early-to-mid 2026, no AI Act-specific notified bodies existed, with designation processes still ongoing across Member States and capacity limited ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). A proposed Commission regulation (COM(2025) 836) would add a new Annex XIV for NANDO integration, but adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
